newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Mubarak talks peace with US, Jordan envoys.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak talks peace with US, Jordan envoys.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak held talks on Saturday with U.S. envoy Dennis Ross on ways to revive the Middle East peace process, officials said.
Ross and Mubarak, who has often mediated in troubled rounds of peace talks, met in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh. Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah also met Mubarak.
Egyptian officials said the U.S. envoy and Mubarak discussed Ross's talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, which lasted late into the night in Palestinian-ruled Ramallah.
Ross and Arafat raised no hopes of an early breakthrough towards ending two months of deadlock sparked by Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Tarawnah met the Egyptian leader separately and said Mubarak and Jordan's King Hussein would meet soon but gave no date or venue.

He added that the results of Ross's visit would become clear only after the envoy had more talks in the region. "Results of Ross's mission so far were not encouraging. But we have to wait for the end of his tour in Egypt and Jordan," he said.
Tarawnah said he hoped for progress in the latest efforts to remove the deadlock and that the U.S. role must be balanced.
"There should be a U.S. balanced initiative that takes into consideration the demands of both parties and not only one side," he told reporters in the resort town in remarks provided to Reuters.

Peace talks between Israel and the PLO collapsed in March when Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu gave the go-ahead for the construction of 6,500 homes for Jews on the East Jerusalem hill called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
The Palestinian Authority cabinet had said in a statement Ross's mission had floundered due to continued construction at the site claimed by both sides.

"The American envoy Dennis Ross did not achieve any progress in his mission with the Israel side as a result of the Israeli government's insistence to continue settlement building in Jabal Abu Ghneim and in other areas," the statement said.
"The Palestinian leadership reiterated to the U.S. envoy the complete rejection of Israeli settlement activities in Jerusalem and its Judaisation," it said.

The PLO says Israel must freeze settlement construction on lands it captured in the 1967 Middle East war before it will return to the negotiating table. Israel demands a Palestinian Authority crackdown on "terror" as a condition to restart talks.
Ross was due to return to Israel and Palestinian self-ruled areas for further meetings after his talks with Mubarak.
